title: Забастовка официанток и запах победы  (The Waitresses' Strike and the Smell of Victory)

segments.t: The next day during lunch service, Nastya runs ragged trying to cover every table in the dining room completely alone because no other waitresses showed up. In the office, Vika smugly asks Chef Barinov if he can smell the sweet scent of her victory.
А вы, пожалуйста, терпите, что хотите делать.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'Enjoy your meal.' Notice how Russian expresses 'pleasant' and 'appetite' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Where are all the other waitresses?' Vika brings out the contrast between 'where' and 'all' in a few short words.
'There is nobody here except me.' In Russian, the idea of 'except' flows naturally into 'there is no' without extra filler words. Vika answers right away.
'What kind of nonsense is this, huh?' In Russian, the idea of 'what' flows naturally into 'and' without extra filler words.
'Well, what can we possibly do about it?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'can'.
'Do you know what we can do?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'know' and finishing on 'can'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Everyone does whatever they can.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'who' and 'what' in a few short words.
А вы, пожалуйста, терпите, что хотите делать.
'And you, please, just endure it and do whatever you want.' Vika anchors the line on 'and', while 'what is one to do' completes the thought.
'What is going to happen to us anyway?' Chef Viktor raises the pitch on 'will be' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Vika answers right away.
'So, do we have a deal?' Vika anchors the line on 'come on', while 'agreed' completes the thought.
'That is none of your business.' In Russian, the idea of 'not' flows naturally into 'matter' without extra filler words.
'Do you smell that scent in the air?' The meaning hinges on 'you' working together with 'the smell' in spoken Russian. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'That is the sweet smell of our victory.' The grammar packs 'this' and 'victory' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
А вы, пожалуйста, терпите, что хотите делать.

When you watch Scene 15 of Episode 19, listen out for the exchange around the waitresses' strike and the smell of victory — you will recognize every Russian phrase right away. See you in the next scene.
